headline: On 6 small checked tasks x 2 repetitions both arms passed 12/12 on the first attempt (no escalation needed), and the router's tier choice cost $0.97 against $1.51 for all-Sonnet (-35%, price-weighted; raw tokens the same, 3.25M). The whole saving is the two lookup tasks sent to Haiku (-95%); in the other 8 pairs B ran on Sonnet like A, and Jev never lowered a tier. The README's "14% of opus cost" is stale (current rules route 11 of 18 bench prompts to Sonnet), so it is not reproduced. Top fix: re-run the routing benchmark on the current prompts and pin ruleTier to it with a test, then make the "checked" rule ignore test globs.

arms.name: Every case agent on Sonnet 5.5 (default), no router
Model per case from route.mjs (rules + Jev live, gate+sc, k=3, apply) with escalate-once cascade
arms.model: router output: haiku (e1-locate, e2-count), sonnet (the rest)

evaluation.planVersion: design.md (frozen before step 6; amended after the review)
evaluation.datasetVersion: bench/tasks e1-locate, e2-count, r1-rename, f1-paginate, d3-maplimit, d5-deps (agents get files/ only)
evaluation.tokenScope: all tokens of each case agent's session (input + output + cache read + cache write) from its subagent transcript; usage.cost is the same tokens at the tool's list prices (Opus 4/20, Sonnet 2/10, Haiku 0.10/0.50 USD per MTok; cache read 0.20/0.20/0.01; cache write 1.25x input). The report's token card is the raw unweighted sum; the price-weighted cost is in evidence/cost.json and the headline.
deviations: Exception to the retro brief, by the user's instruction: the case agents' model is the variable, not forced to Haiku. A = all Sonnet 5.5, B = the tier route.mjs returned for each exact prompt (Jev live, gate+sc, k=3, apply); effort xhigh in both. The reviewer ran on opus.

Weighted cost A $1.505 -> B $0.972 (-35%). Raw tokens 3,255,897 -> 3,254,509 (the report's "Tokens" card is unweighted and shows no change). Haiku:Sonnet price ratio per token is 1:20 (input 0.1:2, output 0.5:10).

B differs from A in only 4 of 12 runs (e1-locate and e2-count, both repetitions, on Haiku). In the other 8 runs B used Sonnet, the same setup as A, so those pairs measure run-to-run noise (A $0.98 vs B $0.94). The saving rests on two trivial lookup tasks. The router was asked with the task's declared type (Explore for e1/e2) as bench.mjs does, while the agents ran as general-purpose (the tool's own pilot did the same); a real Explore subagent may already default to a cheaper model.

Rules and Jev: rule tier haiku for e1/e2/r1, sonnet for f1/d3/d5; Jev voted haiku x3 for e1/e2, sonnet x3 for r1/d3/d5 and sonnet/haiku/sonnet for f1; gate+sc = max, so Jev raised r1-rename from haiku to sonnet (both repetitions) and never lowered a tier. All 12 routes returned a tier, 0 fallbacks; 3 Jev calls per route, 0.7-1.5 s each route.
The cascade never fired: all 24 agents passed the task check on the first attempt, so there is no escalation cost. The pass rate is first-attempt for both arms (A had no retry; B would have had one).

No answer-key leak found: subagent_usage --forbid counted 0 forbidden tool calls for all 24 agents, and a supplementary scan of tool results (scan_results.mjs, added after the review) found 0 hits. The hidden tests and solutions stay inside the repo the agents could read; only the prompt told them to stay in their folder. There is no arm-A contamination check for the skill itself because the tool is the tier choice.

Review (opus, read-only): 2 Critical, 4 Major, 5 Minor, 1 Suggestion. Tool findings (README numbers stale after the prompt rewrite, rules and benchmark tuned on each other, self-consistency falls back to one vote when calls fail) were accepted by the user for this run and not fixed. Measurement-design findings were handled: leak scan added, retry asymmetry noted (never triggered). The Critical finding that B equals A in 8 of 12 runs is a property of the router output and is stated here, not changed.
Orchestrator tokens and the Jev routing calls (about $0.00005 each) are not in either arm's cost; both favour B and would not change the sign here.

Tool and workflow were read from commit cf8b85f of main; the step-7b patch from reports/skill-tool-lifecycle/pending was applied to this worktree's build-skill-tool-workflow and is not part of this experiment's commit.
